The Logger interface and UtilityFactory.create_logger exist to make the logging backend pluggable, but StandardLogger is the only implementation that has ever existed: `grep -r '(Logger)'` returns only `class StandardLogger(Logger)`. The 'cloudwatch' and 'elasticsearch' branches only raise NotImplementedError and are unreachable in practice: every call site of create_logger( passes literal 'standard' or no argument. StandardLogger just forwards message+context strings to jaclang.cli.console.info/error/warning/print, functionality Python's stdlib logging module already provides natively (levels, extra= for structured context, handlers). The interface, factory dispatch, and dead vendor branches could be deleted in favor of direct logging calls, the pattern already used throughout the rest of the codebase (broker.jac, publisher.jac, prometheus_metrics.jac, redis.jac).

breaker.jac hand-rolls a classic CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN circuit breaker state machine as a module-level dict guarded by a threading.Lock (breaker_should_skip/breaker_record_success/breaker_record_failure), used only by rpc/rpc.jac's service_call()/walker_call(). This is a well-known pattern with maintained libraries (e.g. pybreaker) providing the same trip-threshold/cooldown/half-open semantics with thread-safety and state introspection out of the box, instead of a custom dict-based state machine call sites must remember to update correctly. Confirmed via grep across toml/txt/cfg files that no such library is currently a dependency, so this trades ~70 lines of manually-tested concurrency-sensitive logic for one new dependency.

factory.jac ships a full plugin system (a global _registry dict, a public register() API, and _import_dotted() supporting 'module:Class' and 'module.path.Class' syntaxes) to select an Emailer backend at runtime, but the only Emailer subclass shipped in the actual package is SMTPEmailer. Grepped the whole repo for (Emailer) subclasses: only SMTPEmailer in production code, plus test-only _RecordingEmailer/FakeEmailer and an out-of-scope example SendGridEmailer. Grepped callers of register( outside its own definition: exactly one, in a test file, zero production call sites. create() in factory.jac already special-cases the string 'smtp' directly, so the registry/dynamic-import machinery (~35 lines) only ever gets exercised by tests.

LocalEventStream._handle_with_retry (streams/local.jac) and RedisEventStream._handle_with_retry (streams/redis.jac) are a near-verbatim ~35-line retry/backoff loop (same coroutine-rejection check, same warning log format, same wait_or_stop/backoff logic, same DLQ-on-exhaustion flow), differing only in that the Redis version also calls self.ack(event). Both postinit methods also share an identical ~8-line block reading config['retry'] and rebuilding a RetryPolicy default. Read both files in full and confirmed the bodies are structurally identical apart from the ack() calls. streams/_stream_common.jac already exists specifically to hold logic shared between these two brokers (consumer_loop, wait_or_stop), so this retry-handling logic is the piece that should have been extracted there too but wasn't.

ProcessGateway.setup() only builds a MicroserviceGateway with the same constructor args and calls its setup(); ProcessGateway.serve() only lazily calls setup() then self._gateway.start() - no logic of its own is added in the 37-line file. Grepped ProcessGateway and found its only instantiation sites are orchestrator.jac's start_local and start_gateway_only, which always construct the concrete ProcessGateway type directly (never through the Gateway interface), so the wrapper adds no polymorphism either. Orchestrator could construct MicroserviceGateway(...) directly and call .setup()/.start(), removing this indirection entirely.

Port-in-use retry logic is implemented twice, independently. serve.core.impl.jac's _find_available_port probes a raw socket in a loop, incrementing current_port and catching OSError with named errno constants (ERRNO_ADDR_IN_USE_LINUX/WINDOWS declared in server/serve.jac). jserver/impl/jfast_api.impl.jac's run_server runs an essentially identical increment-and-retry loop around uvicorn.Server.run(), but re-hardcodes the same errno values as literals (98, 10048) instead of importing the existing constants, and duplicates the exact warning message shape. Read both loops fully; both do 'try bind/run, on address-in-use bump the port and retry, otherwise re-raise, raise OSError after max_retries' - the same algorithm maintained twice with magic numbers copy-pasted. One retry layer is also redundant at runtime since JacAPIServerCore.start() already calls _find_available_port() before run_server() runs its own retry loop.

A byte-formatting helper using the same magic constants (1073741824, 10737418.24, 1048576, 10485.76, 1024, 10.24) is defined independently in three page files: MetricsPage.cl.jac (formatBytes), GraphsPage.cl.jac (formatBytes), and WorkloadsPage.cl.jac (formatBytes). Read all three and confirmed they compute identical GB/MB/KB/B breakpoints with identical divisor constants, differing only in local variable names. The codebase already has a shared ui/utils/api.cl.jac module used by many pages, so this formatter should live there once instead of being copy-pasted three times.

JacAPIServerStatic.serve_static_file and JacAPIServerStatic.serve_root_asset contain the exact same 8-line block resolving base_path_dir via Jac.get_context()/find_project_root and deriving file_name from Path(file_path).name, verbatim. Both functions then each run their own near-identical 'for candidate_file in [...]: if exists and is_file: read bytes, mimetypes.guess_type, default octet-stream, return Response(...)' loop, differing only in the candidate list and an extra Cache-Control header in the second copy. Read both functions fully end-to-end to confirm the logic (not just shape) is identical. This can be collapsed into one _resolve_base_path() helper and one shared _serve_first_existing(candidates, headers=None) helper.

The block that builds a Trigger (and optional TriggerAuth) from a raw trigger dict is copy-pasted verbatim three times: once in KubernetesTarget.deploy and twice in KubernetesMicroserviceTarget.apply_manifests (for cfg.get('triggers') and effective_extra respectively). Confirmed via grep across deploy/ that all three hits are byte-for-byte identical: construct Trigger(type=str(raw.get('type','')), metadata=dict(raw.get('metadata', {})), name=raw.get('name')), then conditionally attach TriggerAuth(secret_refs=dict(raw_auth.get('secret_refs', {}))), then append. A small _trigger_from_raw(raw: dict) -> Trigger helper would replace all three copies with a one-line call each.
snippet:
t = Trigger(
                    type=str(raw.get("type", "")),
                    metadata=dict(raw.get("metadata", {})),

summary: Gateway is an abstract base (setup()/serve() both raise NotImplementedError) meant to let callers treat gateway implementations polymorphically, but grepping the whole repo for 'Gateway)'/': Gateway'/'-> Gateway' shows only two obj declarations reference it (EmbeddedGateway, ProcessGateway) and zero call sites anywhere type a parameter or variable as Gateway - every caller (orchestrator.jac) uses concrete ProcessGateway/MicroserviceGateway types directly. MicroserviceGateway, the only Gateway-shaped class actually used to serve real traffic, does not even inherit from Gateway (it inherits from the admin mixins instead), so the interface doesn't unify the real implementations. Deleting the base class and inlining setup/serve on each concrete class would lose nothing.

LogsPage.cl.jac (serviceColor) and TracesPage.cl.jac (serviceColorBar) each implement the exact same hand-rolled djb2-style string hash over a 10-entry color palette to pick a stable per-service color. Read both functions in full and confirmed the hashing algorithm and palette length/ordering are identical, differing only in the Tailwind class prefix (text-* vs bg-*). This hashing+lookup logic should be extracted into one shared helper instead of being reimplemented in both pages; TracesPage's own docstring even calls out matching LogsPage's palette intentionally.

Injector is a base class whose four methods (prepare, seed, mutate_pod_spec, extra_manifests) exist purely to be overridden, but it has exactly one subclass in the repo (PvcInjector), which itself has exactly one subclass (BinaryInjector) that is the only one ever instantiated in production code (select_injector always builds a BinaryInjector). Confirmed with grep for '(Injector)' (only PvcInjector(Injector) and BinaryInjector(PvcInjector) match) and for ': Injector'/'-> Injector' (zero matches anywhere) - the base class is never even used as a type annotation; only PvcInjector is referenced as a type. The three-level hierarchy for one real production class collapses safely into a single PvcInjector/BinaryInjector without an interface layer.

The set of framework-reserved path segments (walker, function, user, sso, api-key, webhook, ws, jobs, graph, plus health/metrics/docs variants) is hand-maintained independently in three places: discovery/route_policy.jac's _RESERVED_SEGMENTS (17 entries), gateway/dispatch.jac's _PASSTHROUGH_SEGMENTS/_SERVICE_MEMBER_SEGMENTS, and gateway/microservice_gateway.impl.jac's _BUILTIN_PREFIXES/_BUILTIN_EXACT tuples. Read all three definitions in full: they overlap heavily (walker/function/user/sso/api-key/webhook/ws/jobs/graph appear in all three) but none imports from another, and each has slightly different membership. A future addition of a new builtin route requires updating three separate literals with no compiler check they stay consistent - route_policy.jac's is_reserved() could already silently diverge from dispatch.jac's classify_route().

MiddlewareRegistry.run()/_invoke() hand-implement an onion-style async middleware chain, but no production code calls .run(. Grepped '.run(request'/'registry.run(' across all .jac files: the only callers are unit tests calling it directly to test the chain in isolation. Both real gateways (embedded_gateway.impl.jac, microservice_gateway.impl.jac) only call .install(app), which hands each registered Middleware straight to Starlette's own add_middleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware, ...) - i.e. production requests never traverse the custom _invoke recursion; Starlette's own ASGI middleware stack does the chaining. run/_invoke are reinvented chaining logic that only exists to be unit tested.

SmallSelect is exported from Select.cl.jac but has zero callers. Grepped the entire repository for 'SmallSelect' across all .jac files and the only match is its own definition; every page that needs a compact/inline select (LogsPage, TracesPage) instead hand-rolls its own <select className="..."> markup rather than using this component. Safe to delete.

The helper _s(v) (return '' for None, else str(v)) is defined verbatim in three impl files: deploy_health.impl.jac, network.impl.jac, and podenv.impl.jac. Read all three definitions and confirmed the bodies are byte-identical (only the docstring text differs). Grepping the whole admin/impl tree for 'def _s(v: any) -> str' returns exactly these three hits, each used only within its own file's reshape helpers. This 6-line utility belongs in one shared module (e.g. k8s_ops.jac, which all three files already import from) instead of being copy-pasted three times.

TelemetryStore.get_traces and TelemetryStore.get_trace each independently build an identical parent-id-to-children index by iterating list(self._traces.values()) and grouping by parent_invocation_id. Read both method bodies in full and confirmed the ~8-line loop body is logically and textually identical (only the source-list variable name differs). Since _aggregate_descendants already accepts a children_lookup: dict parameter, this index-building loop should be factored into one private helper (e.g. _build_children_lookup(self)) called from both methods.

formatLatency is defined identically in LLMMetricsPage.cl.jac and LLMTracesPage.cl.jac - read both and the 6-line bodies (ms>=1000 -> seconds with one decimal, else milliseconds rounded) are byte-for-byte the same. Both pages already import shared helpers from ....services.llmService and ....utils.api, so this formatter belongs in one shared utils module instead of being duplicated across the two LLM telemetry pages.

CardBody is exported from Card.cl.jac but has zero callers. Grepped the entire repository for 'CardBody' across all .jac files and the only match is its own definition; no page or component imports or renders it (UsersPage, the only consumer of Card/CardHeader/StatsCard from this file, renders its own <DataTable> directly instead of CardBody). Safe to delete.

EmbeddedGateway (embedded_gateway.jac + embedded_gateway.impl.jac) and InProcessTransport (in transport/transport.jac) form an in-process gateway path with no production caller. Grepped `EmbeddedGateway` and `InProcessTransport` across every .jac file in the repo: the only hits outside their own definitions are tests/microservices/test_embedded_gateway.jac and test_runtime_integration.jac. planner.jac computes a gateway_mode of 'embedded' vs 'process', but its only production consumer, local_realizer.jac, merely logs plan.gateway_mode in an f-string and never branches on it. orchestrator.jac (the real production entry point invoked from plugin.jac) unconditionally constructs ProcessGateway regardless of topology, and plugin.jac itself has zero references to 'embedded' anywhere. This is a fully-built, fully-tested, never-wired subsystem safe to delete along with its dedicated test file.

This ~492-line file defines JacScalePluginConfig, a static schema/metadata-description class (get_plugin_metadata, get_config_schema) that re-describes every default already declared in config/impl/config_loader.impl.jac's get_default_config(), as a verbose nested dict. Grepped the whole repo for JacScalePluginConfig and found only its own declaration line — nothing imports, instantiates, or calls its static methods, including its own test suite. Sibling plugin-config classes elsewhere in the monorepo (JacMcpPluginConfig, byllm's) are exercised by jac/tests/cli/test_mcp.jac; this one has zero references anywhere. Entire file can be deleted.

This entire ~55-line file defines three free functions (_transport_response_to_dict, _get_http_status, _transport_response_to_json_response) that convert a TransportResponse into a JSONResponse. Grepped the whole repo for both function names: the only hits are their own definitions in this file — no caller anywhere, and the functions aren't tied to any declared archetype via `impl X.Y` so nothing forward-declares them either. The functionally identical conversion is actually wired in via jserver/impl/jfast_api.impl.jac's `_convert_transport_response_to_json_response`, called 8 times inside JFastApiServer._create_endpoint_function — confirmed by reading both files in full and comparing the dict-shape logic (ok/type/data/error/meta handling is the same). The whole file is a safe, straightforward deletion.

zod, react-router-dom, react-error-boundary, and @tanstack/react-form are declared in [dependencies.npm] but never imported anywhere in admin/ui. Confirmed by grepping all *.cl.jac files under admin/ui for `zod`, `react-router-dom`, `react-error-boundary`, `@tanstack/react-form`, and `ErrorBoundary` — zero matches in application code (README.md mentions react-router-dom only as a generic 'how to add a dependency' example). Routing is actually done manually via `activeTab` state and a PAGE_ROUTES dict in DashboardLayout.cl.jac, not react-router-dom. These four npm packages inflate install size and client bundle surface with no runtime benefit.

react-router-dom = "^6.22.0"
react-error-boundary = "^5.0.0"
zod = "^4.3.6"

summary: GraphsPage.cl.jac and WorkloadsPage.cl.jac contain byte-for-byte identical formatBytes implementations (same GB/MB/KB/B thresholds and magic-constant division math); MetricsPage.cl.jac has the same logic with only cosmetic variable-name differences. Verified via grep -A10 'def formatBytes' across admin/ui, which surfaced three near-identical bodies. admin/ui/utils/ already exists as a shared-helpers location but none of these three files use it for this function. Collapsing to one shared formatBytes in utils/ removes two of the three copies.

LogsPage.cl.jac's serviceColor and TracesPage.cl.jac's serviceColorBar both implement the exact same string-hash algorithm over a 10-entry Tailwind color palette to assign a stable color per service name, differing only in the CSS class prefix (text-* vs bg-*). TracesPage.cl.jac's own doc-comment explicitly acknowledges it 'matches LogsPage palette' rather than sharing code with it. Verified via grep for the hash expression `(hash<<5)-hash+charCode`, which appears in exactly these two files. Should be one shared helper in admin/ui/utils/ taking a class-prefix parameter.

K8sRuntimeServiceResolver implements the 9-method ServiceDeployer interface, but 8 of those methods (deploy_service, stop_service, restart_service, scale_service, status, get_logs, deploy_all, destroy_all) are stub bodies that just log 'admin op not yet wired' and return False/empty. Grepped the whole repo for `K8sRuntimeServiceResolver(` (constructor call) — the only match is the class declaration itself; it is never instantiated anywhere in production code or tests. Only the free function build_k8s_registry in the same file is actually used (from plugin.jac). The class can be deleted; build_k8s_registry can stay or be simplified separately.

UtilityFactory.create_logger(logger_type, config) string-dispatches to 'standard', 'cloudwatch', or 'elasticsearch', but the latter two branches are literal `raise NotImplementedError(...)` — code paths that can never succeed. Grepped every call site of create_logger repo-wide (runtime/realizer/kubernetes_realizer.jac:75, plugin.jac:266, plugin.jac:319) — all three pass the literal 'standard'; grepping config/ for `logger_type` returns zero results, so nothing ever selects a different value. Additionally Logger (observability/logger.jac) is an abstract interface with exactly one subclass, StandardLogger — grepped `(Logger)` across all .jac files and found only standard_logger.jac. The interface, factory, and two guaranteed-throw branches add indirection with zero behavioral coverage; a bare StandardLogger() call would suffice.

download_release_binary (lines ~111-126) and _admin_dist_urls (lines ~310-326) both fetch the GitHub latest-release metadata, json.loads the body, then loop meta.get('assets', []) filtering names starting with 'jac-' and splitting into a checksum_url (suffix + '.sha256') vs primary url. Read both functions in full within the same file — the logic is line-for-line identical except for the local variable name (binary_url vs dist_url). Extractable into one `_find_release_asset(meta, suffix) -> tuple[str, str]` helper.

Gateway is an abstract base declaring a middleware field and setup()/serve() stubs. Only two classes ever extend it: EmbeddedGateway (confirmed dead in a separate finding) and ProcessGateway. Grepped `self\.middleware` repo-wide: ProcessGateway.setup()/.serve() never reference it (the only non-gateway.jac hit is inside the dead embedded_gateway.impl.jac). ProcessGateway itself does nothing but construct an internal MicroserviceGateway with the same constructor args and forward .serve() to .start(). MicroserviceGateway — the class that does all real routing/admin-API/tracing/metrics/middleware work — does not inherit Gateway at all. With EmbeddedGateway dead, the interface has exactly one live implementation that is a pure pass-through wrapper; orchestrator.jac could construct MicroserviceGateway directly and both gateway.jac and process_gateway.jac could be deleted.

MiddlewareRegistry.run()/_invoke() hand-roll a recursive call-next middleware chain. Grepped `\.run\(request|registry\.run\(` repo-wide: the only callers are in test_middleware.jac and test_runtime_integration.jac. Every production caller — microservice_gateway.impl.jac (the real gateway) and the dead embedded_gateway.impl.jac — only calls `self.middleware.install(app)`, which registers each Middleware.handle directly via `app.add_middleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware, dispatch=middleware.handle)` and lets Starlette do the onion-chaining itself. The hand-rolled _invoke(index, request, handler) chain duplicates what add_middleware already does and is exercised only by unit tests calling run() directly instead of going through install().

route_policy.jac's _RESERVED_SEGMENTS (17 entries), gateway/dispatch.jac's _PASSTHROUGH_SEGMENTS (9 entries), and microservice_gateway.impl.jac's _BUILTIN_PREFIXES (10 entries, including 'cl' which appears in no other list) all independently encode 'which path segments are reserved for the platform, not a user microservice' and have already drifted apart. Read all three files in full to confirm the overlap and divergence. Worse, dispatch.classify_route()'s ROUTE_PASSTHROUGH/ROUTE_STATIC branches (built from _PASSTHROUGH_SEGMENTS) are never actually consulted by microservice_gateway.impl.jac's dispatcher, which only checks ROUTE_BUILTIN/ROUTE_ADMIN/ROUTE_PROXY and then re-derives passthrough/static routing independently via the separate _BUILTIN_PREFIXES list — grepped `ROUTE_STATIC|ROUTE_PASSTHROUGH` repo-wide and outside dispatch.jac itself only tests and the dead embedded_gateway.jac reference these constants.
snippet: glob _PASSTHROUGH_SEGMENTS: set[str] = {"walker","function","user","sso","api-key","webhook","ws","jobs","graph"};

summary: service_call() (lines ~74-114) and walker_call() (lines ~168-201) each independently implement the identical attempt-loop shape: max_attempts=3, backoff=0.1 doubling on httpx.RequestError/httpx.TimeoutException, with breaker_record_success/breaker_record_failure bookkeeping around it. Read the full file — the only difference between the two loops is the HTTP call made inside (client.stream vs client.post) and response unwrapping (_unwrap_sv_envelope vs _hydrate_walker_envelope). The ~20-line retry/backoff/breaker scaffolding in each could be factored into one shared helper taking a callable.

JServer is a full ABC/Generic[T] interface with 5 abstract HTTP-verb methods plus create_server/run_server. Grepped `\(JServer` across all .jac files and found exactly one subclass in the whole codebase: JFastApiServer(JServer[FastAPI]) in jserver/jfast_api.jac. Also grepped for JServer used as a type annotation outside jserver.jac/jserver.impl.jac and found none — nothing treats servers polymorphically through this interface; every caller (server/impl/serve.core.impl.jac etc.) uses JFastApiServer concretely. The ABC buys nothing today; JFastApiServer could absorb init/add_endpoint/execute directly and the abstract methods could be dropped.

prepare_inprocess_runtime takes transport_kind: str = "testclient" and immediately raises NotImplementedError for any other value, citing reserved-for-later values 'asgi'/'isolated_worker'. Grepped transport_kind across all .jac files: it has exactly two call sites (tests/scale_test_client.jac and runtimelib/client/targets/desktop/native/inprocess_dispatch.jac), and both explicitly pass transport_kind="testclient" — identical to the default — so the parameter currently does nothing except carry a placeholder branch for unbuilt future values. A speculative config knob with exactly one real, always-default value.

Injector is an abstract base (4 methods, 3 raising NotImplementedError) meant to let injection strategies be swapped in. Grepped the whole repo for the module path jaclang.scale.injector.injector and found exactly one importer: pvc_injector.jac, which declares `obj PvcInjector(Injector)`. Further grepped for the bare name Injector used as a type annotation in caller code (manifest_builder.jac, kubernetes_target.jac) and found none — callers always type against the concrete PvcInjector/BinaryInjector classes, never the interface. Exactly one concrete implementation chain (PvcInjector -> BinaryInjector) exists, so the interface provides no real polymorphism and could be dropped.

PersistenceType enum and the _persistence_type field are write-only. Grepped the entire repo for `_persistence_type` and `PersistenceType`: the only hits are the declaration and 4 assignment sites, all inside memory_hierarchy.main.impl.jac's postinit. No code anywhere reads self._persistence_type or compares against any PersistenceType member — not in admin/deploy_health, not in logs, not in tests. The enum and field exist purely to be set and never consumed.

parse_memory_quantity and parse_storage_quantity are two hand-rolled, nearly-duplicate implementations of Kubernetes-quantity-string parsing (binary/decimal Ki/Mi/.../K/M suffixes) living in the same file, and kubernetes_redis.jac's _parse_size_to_bytes is a third, independently written parser with yet another non-standard unit table. Worse, the {prometheus_name}-sa ServiceAccount is deleted twice in the same destroy() call — once via the manual try/except near the top and again via delete_if_exists near the bottom — confirmed by reading the full method start to end. Converting the manual blocks to delete_if_exists and removing the duplicate delete is mechanical and low-risk.

DeploymentResult.is_successful() and ResourceStatusInfo.is_ready() (resource_status.jac) are convenience wrapper methods. summary: MongoDb.get, MongoDb.delete, and MongoDb.exists each independently reimplement 'try the key as a raw string _id, and if that misses, retry as an ObjectId' using the shared _as_object_id helper but near-identical surrounding control flow, differing only in which Mongo op is called (find_one/delete_one/count_documents) and how the result is unwrapped. Read all three methods in full to confirm the shape. Could collapse into one shared `_find_with_id_fallback(col, key, op)`-style helper, though the differing return shapes (dict/delete-count/bool) make this less mechanical than other findings.

JacAPIServerCore.start calls _find_available_port(self.port) (a pre-flight test-socket bind loop) before starting the server when there's no prebound listen socket, then calls self.server.run_server(port=self.port). But JFastApiServer.run_server (jfast_api.impl.jac, lines ~151-188) has its own independent retry loop that catches SystemExit/OSError 'Address already in use' from uvicorn.Server.run() and increments the port itself, for the same non-prebound code path. Because the pre-check releases its test socket before uvicorn binds, it doesn't even eliminate the race that run_server's own retry loop exists to handle, so run_server's loop does the real work regardless — confirmed by reading both retry implementations in full. The pre-check's only unique value (an early console message) could be produced from inside run_server's existing loop instead.

DeploymentTargetFactory only ever dispatches to two real implementations (kubernetes, kubernetes-microservice, both Kubernetes-backed), and the sibling DatabaseProviderFactory.create in deploy/database/factory.jac only dispatches to two real implementations (kubernetes_mongo, kubernetes_redis). The 'aws'/'gcp'/'aws_documentdb' branches are placeholders that immediately raise NotImplementedError — they add branches and an impression of multi-cloud support without providing any behavior. The .register() extension point on both factories is exercised by tests and is a legitimate seam, not flagged here.
